results.problem: Bit-truncation product approximation of continuous unitary evolution
results.quote: "Theorem" A. Let H be a regulated, \(\sigma\)-sparse Hermitian family on \([0,T]\), with evolution U starting at the identity. If its entrywise k-bit truncation \(H^{(k)}\) is piecewise constant, the induced product W, one exponential per constant piece, satisfies \(\|W-U(T)\|\le\sqrt{2}\sigma 2^{-k}T\).

results.problem: Midpoint product approximation with bounded total variation
results.bound: O(T\ell/\varepsilon) factors and O(log_2(\sigma T/\varepsilon)) bits
results.quote: "Theorem" B. For a regulated, \(\sigma\)-sparse Hermitian family H on \([0,T]\) with total variation \(0<\ell<\infty\), holding truncated midpoint samples between equal-variation checkpoints gives a product within \(\varepsilon\) of U(T), with \(O(T\ell/\varepsilon)\) factors and \(O(log_2(\sigma T/\varepsilon))\) bits as \(\varepsilon\rightarrow 0\).

u)/T)\).

results.problem: Fine-step adiabatic theorem via midpoint products
results.quote: Corollary 3.15. ... Then W has (k+1)-bit generators, \(n\le 1+4\ell T^2/C\) unitary factors, and leakage \(\|(1-Q)WP\|\le 2C/T\). For a target leakage \(\delta>0\) and \(T=2C/\delta\), provided \(\delta^2\le 4\sqrt{2}\sigma C\), the entry precision and the number of unitaries obey \(k+1\le 2log_2(1/\delta)+log_2(4\sqrt{2}\sigma C)+2\), \(n\le 1+16\ell C/\delta^2\).

results.problem: Explicit unit-step comparison with frame corrections
results.quote: Theorem 6.4. Let T, H, U, and W_T be as in Definition 6.1. Suppose that H is differentiable, \(\|H'\|\le L\), \(\|H'(s)-H'(s')\|\le 2\nu|s-s'|\), and each sample H(j/T), 0<j<T, is \(\gamma\)-separated of width at most \(\bar{w}\) (Definition 2.8). Then \(\left\|W_T-e^{iH(1)/2}U(T)e^{-iH(0)/2}\right\|\le\frac{c_0L+c_1L^2+c_2\nu}{T}\), with c_i from Definition 6.3, or c_i(w) for width at most w<2\pi.

results.problem: Discrete adiabatic theorem for unit-step products
results.quote: Corollary 6.7. ... Then the product W_T of (6.1) satisfies \(\|(1-Q)W_TP\|\le\frac{J_m(\|H'\|,\|H''\|,g)+c_0L+c_1L^2+c_2\nu}{T}\), with the Jansen-Ruskai-Seiler coefficient J_m of Definition 3.14 and c_i from Definition 6.3.

results.problem: Quantum linear systems via unit-step adiabatic product
results.bound: \|(1-P(1))W_TP(0)\|\le 45\kappa/T, \text{so } \lceil 45\kappa/\delta\rceil \text{ unit steps give leakage at most } \delta
results.quote: Corollary 6.9. ... If \kappa>1, then, for every integer T\ge 1, the product (6.1) satisfies \(\|(1-P(1))W_TP(0)\|\le\frac{5J_1(|f'|,|f''|,g)}{4T}\le\frac{45\kappa}{T}\), with the Jansen-Ruskai-Seiler coefficient J_1 of Definition 3.14. If \kappa=1, then (1-P(1))W_TP(0)=0. Thus, for \delta>0, \lceil 45\kappa/\delta\rceil unit steps give leakage at most \delta.

results.problem: Walk logarithm comparison via free spectral arc
results.quote:

u|s-s'|. Suppose that some open arc of length 2\pi-w meets the spectrum of no W(s). Then there is a differentiable Hermitian path \Lambda on [0,1] with e^{-i\Lambda}=W such that, for the product W_T of the compatible walk and evolution U_\Lambda of \Lambda(t/T),  ig\|W_T-e^{i\Lambda(1)/2}U_\Lambda(T)e^{-i\Lambda(0)/2} ig\|\le rac{c_0L_\Lambda+c_1L_\Lambda^2+c_2
u_\Lambda}{T}, where c_i=c_i(w), L_\Lambda=\mathcal{B}L, and 
u_\Lambda=\mathcal{B}(
u+( rac{1}{2}+\mathcal{B}')L^2), with the Bernoulli majorant \mathcal{B} of Definition 2.8 and its derivative \mathcal{B}' evaluated at w.

results.problem: Quantum linear systems via rescaled qubitized walk
results.bound: \|(I-P(1))W((T-1)/T)\cdots W(0)P(0)\|\le K\kappa/T, \text{so } \lceil K\kappa/\delta\rceil \text{ steps suffice; each attempt uses } N+2\le(2K+3)\kappa/\delta \text{ controlled O queries}
results.quote: Corollary A.2. ... The walk W(s) of Definition A.1 uses one controlled O query per step. For the constant K>0 of Lemma A.4: (1) For every integer T\ge 1, \|(I-P(1))W((T-1)/T)\cdots W(0)P(0)\|\le K\kappa/T, where P(s) projects onto the line through F_sL([(1-f(s))I+f(s)A]^{-1}b,0), a+i eigenvector of W(s). Thus, for 0<\delta\le 1, \lceil K\kappa/\delta\rceil steps suffice for leakage at most \delta. (2) For 0<\delta\le 1, put N=\lceil 2K\kappa/\delta\rceil. ... Each attempt uses N+2\le(2K+3)\kappa/\delta controlled O queries, excluding preparing b, implementing Q_b, and operations built from V .
